# google_apigee_security_settings

Represents the Advanced API Security settings of an Apigee organization.
Manages whether the organization consents to the use of machine learning (ML)
models for abuse detection.


To get more information about SecuritySettings, see:

* [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/reference/apis/apigee/rest/v1/SecuritySettings)
* How-to Guides
    * [Manage the Advanced API Security add-on](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/reference/manage-security-add-on)
    * [Opt in for machine learning models for Abuse Detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-security/abuse-detection#opt-in-for-machine-learning-models-for-abuse-detection)

~> **Note:** Security settings exist only for Apigee organizations that have the Advanced API Security
add-on enabled. For Subscription and Evaluation organizations, enable it with
`google_apigee_addons_config`; for Pay-as-you-go organizations, enable it in at least one
environment. Creating a resource of this type will acquire and update the existing security
settings of the organization. Deleting this resource will remove it from your Terraform
state but leave the security settings as is.


## Example Usage - Apigee Security Settings Basic


```hcl
data "google_client_config" "current" {}

resource "google_compute_network" "apigee_network" {
  name = "apigee-network"
}

resource "google_compute_global_address" "apigee_range" {
  name          = "apigee-range"
  purpose       = "VPC_PEERING"
  address_type  = "INTERNAL"
  prefix_length = 16
  network       = google_compute_network.apigee_network.id
}

resource "google_service_networking_connection" "apigee_vpc_connection" {
  network                 = google_compute_network.apigee_network.id
  service                 = "servicenetworking.googleapis.com"
  reserved_peering_ranges = [google_compute_global_address.apigee_range.name]
}

resource "google_apigee_organization" "apigee_org" {
  analytics_region   = "us-central1"
  project_id         = data.google_client_config.current.project
  authorized_network = google_compute_network.apigee_network.id
  depends_on         = [google_service_networking_connection.apigee_vpc_connection]
}

resource "google_apigee_addons_config" "apigee_org_security_addons_config" {
  org = google_apigee_organization.apigee_org.name
  addons_config {
    api_security_config {
      enabled = true
    }
  }
}

resource "google_apigee_security_settings" "security_settings" {
  org_id                         = google_apigee_organization.apigee_org.id
  ml_retraining_feedback_enabled = true

  depends_on = [
    google_apigee_addons_config.apigee_org_security_addons_config
  ]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `org_id` -
  (Required)
  The Apigee Organization associated with the Apigee Security Settings,
  in the format `organizations/{{org_name}}`.


* `ml_retraining_feedback_enabled` -
  (Optional)
  If true, the user consents to the use of ML models for abuse detection.



## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `{{org_id}}/securitySettings`

* `name` -
  Name of the security settings resource,
  in the format `organizations/{{org_name}}/securitySettings`.

## Import


SecuritySettings can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `{{org_id}}/securitySettings`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import SecuritySettings using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    orgId = "<-required value->"
  }
  to = google_apigee_security_settings.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import SecuritySettings using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "{{org_id}}/securitySettings"
  to = google_apigee_security_settings.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), SecuritySettings can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_apigee_security_settings.default {{org_id}}/securitySettings
```
